title: Superannuation (Excess Concessional Contributions Tax) Amendment (DisabilityCare Australia) Bill 2013

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would increase the tax rate applying to individuals whose concessional superannuation contributions exceed the relevant limits, reflecting the higher Medicare levy.
It would raise the excess contributions tax rate from 31.5 per cent to 32 per cent by increasing the Medicare levy component.
The increase would apply to assessments for the 2014-15 financial year onwards and accompany the wider package of DisabilityCare Australia tax amendments.
changes: The rate charged on excess concessional contributions would rise by half a percentage point.
The calculation would use a Medicare levy component of 2 per cent.
The revised rate would cover assessments for 2014-15 and subsequent financial years.
summary.affected: Individuals making concessional superannuation contributions above the applicable thresholds are affected.

speeches.speaker: Bill Shorten
speeches.brief: Moved the Superannuation (Excess Concessional Contributions Tax) Amendment (DisabilityCare Australia) Bill, explaining that the tax rate on excess concessional contributions would rise from 31.5 per cent to 32 per cent from 1 July 2014 to reflect the Medicare levy increase.

speeches.speaker: Jacinta Collins
speeches.brief: Moved to suspend standing orders so that 14 bills related to DisabilityCare Australia (the National Disability Insurance Scheme) could be considered during the current sitting period; the motion was agreed to.
